fullPassage:
UNESCO King Sejong Literacy Prize

The UNESCO King Sejong Literacy Prize is named after Sejong the Great, who is known for his contributions to the advancement of literacy and the creation of the Korean script, Hangeul. It honors institutions, organizations, or individuals that contribute to the reduction of illiteracy around the world. An example of an organization that received the prize is Ageing Nepal for its Basic Literacy Class for Older Persons program. This program improves the quality of life and rights of senior citizens by providing basic skills in reading and writing in both Nepali and English. Through literacy education, the program enhances the senior citizens' ability to live independently within their local communities. Another recipient is the Center for the Study of Learning and Performance at Concordia University in Canada. The center developed and distributed an interactive learning application for free to promote education. This innovative application has helped increase literacy rates in Africa.
